# Tool Intent Router — QA data

Synthetic QA data for the chat tool intent router and the Google Calendar tool behind it.
No real user data, no real document content, no credentials.

Two files, two different jobs.

---

## `tool_intent_qa.json` — 25 cases, deterministic

The main set. Each case carries the user story, the message, the classifier labels, the route
`finalize_route` produces under that case's own capability context, and — where a tool actually
runs — what the calendar should end up holding.

**Every `expected_final_route` and `expected_appended_reason_codes` value in this file was
generated by running the real `finalize_route`, not by hand.** They are not aspirational; they
are what the shipped resolver does today. When the resolver changes, these values are supposed
to disagree with it — that is the point.

`now` is `2026-08-26T09:00:00+07:00`, a **Wednesday**. Every relative date in the set resolves
against it: "thứ Sáu" is the 28th, "mai" is the 27th, "thứ Hai" is the 31st (next Monday, not
two days ago).

### Fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `tier` | Risk tier — see below. Not a group-balance constraint; add freely. |
| `story` | The user story in plain words, for whoever reads a failure. |
| `context` | `tool_axis_enabled`, `available_tools`, `now`. Varies per case on purpose. |
| `classifier_labels` | What the classifier should emit: the three axes plus `tool_name`. |
| `expected_final_route` | Route after `finalize_route` applies the gates in `context`. |
| `expected_appended_reason_codes` | Only the **server-owned** codes the resolver adds. Classifier-owned codes vary by model and are deliberately not asserted. |
| `expected_tool_outcome` | `null` unless the route is `tool`. Otherwise `events_created` and, where the time is checkable, `expect_start` / `expect_end`. |
| `why_it_matters` | Why this case earns its place. If it does not describe a user-visible harm, it should not be here. |

### Tiers, in descending order of user pain

| Tier | n | What it protects |
|---|---|---|
| `happy_path` | 4 | The feature exists at all, in both languages. |
| `silent_wrong_write` | 4 | A real event created at the wrong time, which the user discovers late or never. |
| `false_positive_write` | 4 | Talking *about* a calendar is not asking for one. A wrong write costs more than a missed one. |
| `compound_request` | 3 | "Based on this document, make me a schedule." See the gap below. |
| `unsupported_verb` | 3 | Move / cancel / repeat. The failure mode is creating something, not doing nothing. |
| `duplicate_write` | 2 | Retry gives one event; two genuine turns give two. |
| `capability_gate` | 3 | Flag off and registry empty — today's actual deployments. |
| `prompt_injection` | 2 | Message text and document text are data, never instructions. |

### The finding worth reading first

`tq-013` is the user's own second story — *"Dựa vào tài liệu này, giúp tôi tạo lịch học"* — and
it exposes a real product gap, not a bug.

The classifier is right to answer `needs_rag=true, needs_tool=true`. But `finalize_route`
collapses `RAG_TOOL` to `TOOL` and clears `effective_needs_rag`, so the event is created with
no document evidence behind it. Nothing errors. The user asked for a study plan derived from
their roadmap and receives a generic calendar block, with no signal that the document was never
read.

`tq-014` makes it worse: with **no** ready documents the outcome is byte-identical, because the
no-ready-documents gate never runs — `RAG_TOOL` was already collapsed before that check. Two
very different situations look the same to the user.

`tq-015` is the counterweight. With the tool axis **off** — today's configuration everywhere —
the same request degrades to pure `RAG` and the user gets a document-grounded plan as text.
That is arguably the better answer. Worth knowing before the flag is turned on.

## `chat_routing_labels_tool_block.json` — 4 cases, not yet merged

The classifier-fixture work from `SPEC-chat-tools-registry` §11, prepared but **deliberately
not appended** to `tests/fixtures/chat_routing/chat_routing_labels.json`.

Two prerequisites have to be met first, and neither is mine to decide.

**1. Group balance forces four cases, not two.** The spec asked for two — a create-event case
and a calendar-mention distractor. The loader rejects an unbalanced set outright
(`chat routing fixture groups must be evenly balanced`) and `test_chat_routing_loader.py`
asserts `set(counts.values()) == {len(cases) // 4}`. So additions come in multiples of four,
one per group, and each group keeps its invariant: `ambiguous` cases must have
`expected_needs_rag=true`, `distractor` cases must have it `false`. The block below satisfies
both.

**2. The evaluator would score two of these as failures even when the classifier is right.**
`scripts/evaluate_chat_routing.py` builds its `ChatRoutingService` with the constructor
defaults — `tool_axis_enabled=False`, `available_tools=()` — so every tool case is narrowed away
before it is scored:

| id | group | labelled | axis on + tool registered | evaluator today |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cr-061` | `obvious_chat` | `tool` | `tool` | **`chat`** |
| `cr-062` | `distractor` | `chat` | `chat` | `chat` |
| `cr-063` | `ambiguous` | `tool` | `tool` | **`rag`** |
| `cr-064` | `obvious_rag` | `rag` | `rag` | `rag` |

Merging the block without passing `tool_axis_enabled=True` and
`available_tools={"create_calendar_event"}` into that service would bake in two guaranteed
failures and make the eval report say the classifier is worse than it is.

**3. Merging costs a live re-run.** 60 cases become 64 live classifier calls. That spend is the
user's to authorize, not a default to take.

### To merge, once those are settled

1. Pass the tool axis and the registry names into `ChatRoutingService` in
   `scripts/evaluate_chat_routing.py`.
2. Append the four cases to `chat_routing_labels.json`.
3. Re-run the labelled set and record the new baseline.

---

## Running the data

`loader.py` is the only thing that parses this JSON. Three callers read it — the offline
suite, the live scorer, and the HTML register — and one loader is what keeps them from
drifting apart. It rejects a missing field, an unknown tier, a classifier-owned reason code,
a naive timestamp, and a case that claims a tool outcome without routing to `tool`.

| What | Where | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Offline suite — routes, gates, guards, write counts | [`tests/unit/features/ai_chat/test_tool_intent_qa.py`](../../unit/features/ai_chat/test_tool_intent_qa.py) | Free; runs in `uv run pytest -q` |
| Loader validation | [`tests/unit/fixtures/test_tool_intent_loader.py`](../../unit/fixtures/test_tool_intent_loader.py) | Free |
| Live scorer — does a model resolve the dates right? | [`scripts/evaluate_tool_intent.py`](../../../scripts/evaluate_tool_intent.py) | ~14 provider calls |

```bash
uv run python scripts/evaluate_tool_intent.py --dry-run
```

Spec, plan, and results: [`docs/evaluations/CHAT/`](../../../docs/evaluations/CHAT/PROGRESS.md).

### One thing to know before consuming this file

Several cases share a `current_message` on purpose — `tq-001`/`tq-019`/`tq-020`, and
`tq-013`/`tq-014`. A retry and a fresh intent *are* the same sentence; only the idempotency
key differs. Any consumer that keys on message text will collapse them. Key on `id`, or on
call order.
